Subject: POC onramp & MAP — next steps

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are keen to run a 30-day POC focused on clinical-note summarization and want to embed Redwood in our pipeline as quickly as possible. Can you send a concise MAP that covers the environment steps we need to close (API keys, org/admin setup, IP allowlist, and VPC peering)?

High-level constraints: EKG is in the US (GCP us-central1), we need SOC2 evidence for prod later, and we have a small security review this Friday. If we can get the POC org and keys by next week, we can start validation.

Who should I expect to work with on the peering/network windows and the allowlist? Also — any preferred formats for the info you need from our side?

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Infrastructure, EKG Health
alex@ekghealth.com

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-05T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC onramp & MAP — next steps

Alex — thanks, excited to run this with EKG.

I put together a compact MAP and a one-page onboarding checklist so we can move quickly. Key milestones (proposed):
- Day 0–2: Org creation and admin invites (we'll provision a POC org in the Redwood Console and add EKG admins).
- Day 3: API key issuance + short-lived SDK creds for staging tests.
- Day 4–6: IP allowlist configuration (we'll need CIDR blocks) + automated prefix caching enabled for summarization workloads.
- Day 5–9: VPC peering window — optional but recommended for throughput-sensitive tests; coordinate maintenance window with EKG networking.
- Day 10–30: Run eval prompts, collect quality metrics, and tune batching/quantization settings.

To keep this tight I attached a MAP spreadsheet (EKG-MAP-master-20280305.xlsx) and a simple network diagram (ekg-network-diagram-v1.pdf). Please fill the sheet column "Network: Allowlist/CIDRs" and the org admin emails.

Questions for you now:
1) Confirm the primary contact for peering (name + email).
2) Share the CIDR ranges you want allowed (public IPs or NAT ranges are fine).
3) Do you prefer us to run an IP-only allowlist first or do you want a VPC peering test in parallel?

I'll loop in Vanessa and Irene from Ops to confirm peering requirements and estimated lead times.

—Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Office: (415) 555-0183

(Attachments: EKG-MAP-master-20280305.xlsx, ekg-network-diagram-v1.pdf)

- Any constraints on ephemeral API key rotation policy for POC (we typically provide a short-lived key + ability to rotate during the POC).

Can you propose earliest available windows for next Tue/Wed? I will relay back to Alex.

Thanks — Sean

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: 2028-03-06T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC onramp & MAP — EKG Health (ask for peering window)

Sean — we can support peering in us-central1. Quick answers:
- Preferred approach: start with IP allowlist + API keys so they can run smoke tests immediately. Schedule VPC peering for a follow-up 2–3 day window once initial tests pass.
- ASN: 64512 (private ASN for peering).
- BGP: we support static and BGP sessions; for the POC static routes are easiest. If EKG wants BGP we'll collect ASN + neighbor IPs and set up a test BGP session.
- Lead time: we can provision a peering and run internal checks within 48 hours of confirmed window; please allow 1 business day for us to schedule engineers.
- API key policy: we'll issue a POC key with 30-day TTL and rotation endpoint; we recommend rotating keys mid-POC (day 15) to validate key rollovers.

I'll block Tue 2028-03-14 09:00–11:00 PT and Wed 2028-03-15 13:00–15:00 PT as candidate windows. If Alex prefers earlier, we can try to move resources but it may add risk.

Vanessa Ortiz
Cloud Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
